logo.rights: Official university brand asset served from the university's own media domain and used for factual identification; no ownership transfer or open licence claimed.

cover.altText: Aerial view of the Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research campus at Porur, Chennai

universities.summary: Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research (SRIHER) is a private deemed-to-be university on a 150-acre campus at Porur, Chennai. Its 15 faculties span medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, nursing, physiotherapy, allied health, public health, psychology, management and engineering around a teaching hospital. Indian applicants use SRIHER's own entrance or interview routes and NEET counselling for medical seats; foreign nationals and NRIs apply through its International Relations Office.
universities.campusLifestyle: The 150-acre Porur campus holds 15 constituent faculties, a teaching hospital the university reports at more than 2,500 beds, a 40,000 sq ft central library open 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. on working days, a swimming pool, playgrounds, a bank with ATMs, a post office, a railway reservation counter and multi-cuisine restaurants. Student life runs through 16 clubs including dance, debate, fitness, Rotaract, Tamil, English literature, theatre and yoga, six NSS units, and Army and Naval NCC wings. SRIHER reports an alumni network of more than 20,000 graduates.
universities.cityProfile: SRIHER is at Porur in western Chennai, the capital of Tamil Nadu on India's south-east coast, with the postal address Porur, Chennai 600 116. The campus works as a self-contained township with colleges, staff quarters, a medical centre, the university hospital, retail stores and a travel service, so most day-to-day needs are met on site. Foreign nationals complete Foreigners Regional Registration Office formalities in Chennai after admission, with the university filing the residence and student registrations. First-year teaching starts in July: for 2026-27 entrants, undergraduate classes were scheduled to begin around the second week of July and postgraduate classes around the third week, with exact dates emailed to admitted students in advance.
universities.practicalExposure: Clinical and field training is built around Sri Ramachandra Hospital, a tertiary care and referral centre inside the campus that the university reports sees an average of 5,000 out-patients a day. The Bachelor of Physiotherapy is offered under the NCAHP allied and healthcare professions framework, with fourth-year clinical rotations and a one-year internship across musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiology and ICU, pulmonology, sports, obstetric, paediatric, oncology and burns physiotherapy. The Bachelor of Occupational Therapy includes supervised clinical training or field work in every academic year before a one-year compulsory rotatory internship. The M.Sc. Clinical Psychology includes two clinical rotations, psychological assessment practicals and a dissertation. The Master of Public Health is run by the Faculty of Public Health, whose Department of Environmental Health Engineering has been a WHO Collaborating Centre for occupational health since 2007 and started the MPH in collaboration with the University of California, Berkeley; students add a field practicum, a dissertation and an internship. The MBA in Hospital and Health Systems Management includes two hands-on hospital postings, a summer internship and a dissertation. SRIHER's placement cell reports about 700 offers through 230 campus processes in its latest cycle, with packages from INR 2.2 lakh to INR 72 lakh a year.
universities.hostelOverview: International students live in separate hostels for men and women inside the campus, with wardens assigned to international residents. For 2026-27 the published international hostel rates are USD 1,700 a year for an air-conditioned single room with common bath (USD 750 one-time caution deposit), USD 900 for an air-conditioned twin share or a non-air-conditioned single (USD 375 deposit each) and USD 450 for a non-air-conditioned twin share (USD 300 deposit). Fees are paid at admission and then annually, and rooms are allotted subject to availability. Hostel entry and exit are logged by biometric readers, entrances are under CCTV, and hostel gates close at 9 p.m.
universities.dietarySupport: Mess and canteen dining is provided inside the hostel complexes, and students pay the mess directly before hostel admission at the rate SRIHER notifies each year; this is not included in the hostel fee. Meals are served only in the mess, with no room service, and night cafeterias in the hostels sell snacks, coffee and tea between 9 p.m. and 1 a.m. Carbonated beverages and junk food are banned on university premises under a Government of India higher-education directive.
universities.safetyOverview: SRIHER applies the UGC, medical, dental and AICTE anti-ragging regulations and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Ragging Act 1997, and reported no ragging incidents in the current year. Health insurance is mandatory for foreign students at USD 50 a year, and the campus hospital runs a 24-hour emergency service with an ambulance, treating students at concessional charges.
universities.studentSupport: The International Relations Office handles foreign-national and NRI admissions, pre-arrival guidance, FRRO registration, Bonafide Certificates and APAAR IDs for students without Aadhaar. Three student counsellors offer free, confidential sessions on the third floor of the IQAC wing, every student is assigned a faculty mentor, and an international student orientation is held on arrival.

faq.question: Is Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research a public or a private university?
faq.answer: SRIHER is a private, not-for-profit, self-financing institution. It began in 1985 as Sri Ramachandra Medical College and Research Institute, set up by the Sri Ramachandra Educational and Health Trust, was declared a Deemed to be University by the Government of India in September 1994 under Section 3 of the UGC Act, and took its current name in August 2018. It is not a state or central government university.

faq.question: Who can apply to SRIHER as an international student?
faq.answer: The Foreign National category covers holders of a foreign passport, including OCI cardholders, and Nepal or Bhutan citizens holding citizenship cards. For postgraduate programmes OCI cardholders may apply only as foreign nationals. Non-Resident Indians and NRI-sponsored candidates use a separate NRI category with its own application and fee table. Applications filed in the wrong category are not considered.

faq.question: Do international applicants sit an entrance examination?
faq.answer: Foreign nationals and NRIs are exempt from SRIHER's own undergraduate and postgraduate entrance examinations for programmes governed by university regulations, unless a programme specifies otherwise, and are admitted on first-cum-first-served merit; SRIHER may hold an online interview. Programmes governed by councils follow those councils' rules, and the 2026-27 application states that admission to NCAHP programmes requiring NEET cannot be confirmed without a valid NEET appearance.

faq.question: What language are SRIHER programmes taught in, and is IELTS or TOEFL required?
faq.answer: Foreign nationals and NRIs are exempt from SRIHER's own undergraduate and postgraduate entrance examinations for programmes governed by university regulations, unless a programme specifies otherwise, and are admitted on first-cum-first-served merit; SRIHER may hold an online interview. Programmes regulated by a health-professions council follow that council's current rules, so confirm the specific programme's entrance and registration conditions before applying.

faq.question: Can I apply with A Levels or the International Baccalaureate?
faq.answer: The programme regulations SRIHER publishes for its health-sciences degrees make English the medium of instruction and examination. The 2026-27 international prospectuses do not list an IELTS or TOEFL requirement; English is assessed through the qualifying examination instead, for example English at AS Level or five IGCSE or GCSE passes including English for A Level applicants, and English as a subject for IB applicants. Where a current prospectus does not state the teaching language for a specific programme, this profile leaves it unstated rather than assuming English.

faq.question: How much does it cost to study at SRIHER as a foreign national?
faq.answer: SRIHER publishes a total programme fee in US dollars. For 2026-27 entrants examples are USD 26,500 for the five-year BPT or BOT, USD 14,000 for the three-year B.Sc. Applied Psychology, USD 7,000 for the two-year MPH and USD 9,500 for the M.Sc. Clinical Psychology. On top come a one-time USD 50 registration fee, USD 50 a year health insurance, university examination fees, hostel from USD 450 to USD 1,700 a year plus a one-time caution deposit, and mess charges.

faq.question: How do I apply to SRIHER from abroad?
faq.answer: SRIHER publishes a total programme fee in US dollars. For 2026-27 entrants examples are USD 26,500 for the five-year BPT or BOT, USD 14,000 for the four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Biomedical Sciences or the three-year B.Sc. Applied Psychology, USD 16,000 for B.Sc. (Hons.) Medical Biotechnology, USD 9,000 for the allied-health B.Sc. (Hons.) umbrella, USD 7,000 for the MPH, USD 9,500 for the M.Sc. Clinical Psychology, USD 12,000 for the Master of Medical Radiology and Imaging Technology and USD 3,500 for the MSW. On top come a one-time USD 50 registration fee, USD 50 a year health insurance, examination fees, hostel and mess charges.

faq.question: When does the SRIHER intake start and when do applications close?
faq.answer: SRIHER admits international students once a year for a July start. For 2026-27 the last date for foreign-national undergraduate applications was 30 June 2026, with classes from around the second week of July, and the last date for NRI and foreign-national postgraduate applications was 10 July 2026, with classes from around the third week of July.

faq.question: What visa and registration steps apply to international students?
faq.answer: Foreign nationals need an Indian student visa, not a tourist visa, and those who need a visa are admitted only once it is issued. Postgraduate foreign-national applicants must register on the Study in India portal, obtain an SII ID and apply for the visa through it. SRIHER registers each foreign student and their campus residence with the FRRO within 24 hours of admission, and students on visas longer than 180 days register with the FRRO within 14 days of arrival.

faq.question: How is SRIHER accredited and ranked?
faq.answer: NAAC accredited SRIHER A++ with a CGPA of 3.53 in its third cycle, declared in January 2021. The National Board of Accreditation lists the B.Pharm at the Faculty of Pharmacy to 30 June 2028 and the MBA in Hospital and Health Management to 30 June 2027. In NIRF 2025 SRIHER ranked 21 st for medical, 13 th for dental, 36 th for pharmacy and 60 th among universities. Professional registration abroad is decided by each country's own licensing body.

faq.question: Where do international students live, and what does accommodation cost?
faq.answer: Separate on-campus hostels for men and women are reserved for international students. The 2026-27 annual rates are USD 1,700 for an air-conditioned single, USD 900 for an air-conditioned twin share or non-air-conditioned single, and USD 450 for a non-air-conditioned twin share, plus a one-time caution deposit of USD 300 to USD 750. Mess charges are paid separately, and rooms are allotted subject to availability.

faq.question: Can foreign nationals study MBBS or BDS at SRIHER?
faq.answer: Not through a published route in 2026-27. SRIHER's foreign-national undergraduate prospectus and application forms for 2026-27 are issued for programmes excluding medical and dental degrees, so MBBS and BDS do not appear among the programmes offered to foreign nationals this cycle. Allied-health, psychology, public-health and management degrees are the programmes with a published international route.

faq.question: What happens to fees if I withdraw from a programme?
faq.answer: SRIHER states that fees paid to the university are not refunded or adjusted. A student who discontinues after the admission cut-off date, or whose seat cannot be refilled, must pay tuition and other fees for the entire remaining programme period, and certificates such as the transfer certificate and mark sheets are withheld until that payment is made.

admissionsContent.overview: Master of Anaesthesia and Operation Theatre Technology is a 2-year regular programme at SRIHER, Porur, Chennai. University entrance examination and the programme-specific qualifying requirements govern this route. Confirm the complete fee category and original-record requirements before acceptance.

eligibility.intro: Use this exact qualifying route and the applicable selection process. Accepted equivalence, original records and any required registration, internship or medical-fitness conditions are assessed by the university or counselling authority.
items: Bachelor of at least 3 years in Anaesthesia/Operation Theatre Technology or accepted related field.
The source separately specifies HSC 50% open/45% reserved; retain that school-level condition, not invented UG marks threshold.

evidence.claimText: Current 2026–27 FN prospectus establishes the qualifying-subject/equivalence and FN application route; no separate NEET requirement or waiver confirmed in the retained brochure.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), pp. 10-11; BPT programme page
evidence.internalNotes: Programme page https://sriramachandra.edu/programme/bachelor-of-physiotherapy-bpt/ read 2026-09-21. The FN prospectus eligibility table for BPT does not itself mention NEET, but the FN UG 2026-27 application (https://media.sriramachandra.edu/ms/storage/2026/02/FN-UG-26-27-application.pdf) states that programmes where NCAHP regulations mandate NEET cannot be confirmed without a valid NEET appearance; the NEET requirement is therefore published as a restriction.

evidence.claimText: Foreign-national UG applications for 2026-27 are submitted by email to the International Relations Office, processed on a first-cum-first-served merit basis with no university entrance examination for university-regulated programmes, followed by a provisional offer, first-instalment payment, a confirmation letter, student visa, document verification and FRRO registration.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), pp. 8, 18-19

evidence.claimText: The 2026-27 FN UG prospectus sets 30 June 2026 as the last date for applications and states first-year classes usually commence around the second week of July 2026.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), pp. 18, 21

evidence.claimText: SRIHER's BPT regulations state that English shall be the medium of instruction for all courses of study and for examinations of the Bachelor of Physiotherapy programme.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER BPT regulations (IQAC portal, archived)
evidence.internalNotes: The regulations were published on SRIHER's former IQAC document portal (iqac.sriramachandra.edu.in), which no longer resolves after the move to sriramachandra.edu; the official PDF was read from the Internet Archive copy on 2026-09-21.

evidence.claimText: SRIHER's 2026-27 Foreign Nationals UG prospectus requires for BOT a 10+2 pass with 50 per cent aggregate in Physics, Chemistry and Biology (Botany and Zoology); candidates who studied abroad must hold an equivalent qualification determined under UGC guidelines and have passed Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English at 12 th-standard level; age 17 by 31 December 2026; and a physical fitness certificate at admission.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), pp. 11-12
evidence.internalNotes: BOT programme page (https://sriramachandra.edu/programme/bachelor-of-occupational-therapy-bot/) states 5 years (4 years academics plus 1 year CRI) and PO 4 references the NCAHP Act. The FN UG 2026-27 application (https://media.sriramachandra.edu/ms/storage/2026/02/FN-UG-26-27-application.pdf) says NEET is required for certain NCAHP programmes as indicated in the prospectus; the prospectus BOT row does not name NEET, so the requirement is carried only as a conditional restriction.

evidence.claimText: Foreign-national UG applications for 2026-27 are emailed to the International Relations Office and processed on a first-cum-first-served merit basis, with the steps provisional offer, fee payment, confirmation letter, student visa, document verification and FRRO registration.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), pp. 8, 18-19

evidence.claimText: The 2026-27 FN UG prospectus sets 30 June 2026 as the last date for applications and states first-year classes usually commence around the second week of July 2026.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), pp. 18, 21

evidence.claimText: SRIHER's BOT regulations state that English shall be the medium of instruction for all subjects of study and that examinations will be conducted only in English.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER BOT regulations and syllabus 2020-21 (IQAC portal, archived)
evidence.internalNotes: The regulations were published on SRIHER's former IQAC document portal (iqac.sriramachandra.edu.in), which no longer resolves after the move to sriramachandra.edu; the official PDF was read from the Internet Archive copy on 2026-09-21.

evidence.claimText: SRIHER began in 1985 as Sri Ramachandra Medical College and Research Institute, a not-for-profit self-financing institution of the Sri Ramachandra Educational and Health Trust; the Government of India declared it a Deemed to be University in September 1994 under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956, and it was renamed Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research in August 2018.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), p. 4
evidence.internalNotes: The former domain www.sriramachandra.edu.in now serves a 'We've moved' redirect page to https://sriramachandra.edu (checked 2026-09-21), which is why the first-audit international pages returned ~300-character stubs. UGC deemed-university list not separately fetched; no UGC badge is claimed.

evidence.claimText: SRIHER has 15 constituent faculties including medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, nursing, physiotherapy, allied health sciences, management sciences, biomedical sciences and technology, public health, sports and exercise sciences, clinical research, engineering and technology, audiology and speech language pathology, occupational therapy and behavioural and social sciences, on a 150-acre campus at Porur, Chennai.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), p. 5

evidence.claimText: The campus spreads over 150 acres with a hospital of over 2,500 beds, central library, auditorium, swimming pool, playgrounds, multi-cuisine restaurants, bank with ATMs, retail stores, travel service, railway reservation counter and post office; SRIHER houses 16 clubs (dance, debate, fitness, Rotaract, Tamil, English literature, theatre, yoga etc.), 6 NSS units, Army and Naval NCC wings and an alumni network of over 20,000 graduates.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), pp. 5-6
evidence.internalNotes: Library area 40,000 sq ft and hours 8 a.m.-10 p.m. working days from the Student Manual 2026-27 (https://media.sriramachandra.edu/ms/storage/2026/07/Student-Manual-2026-27.pdf) and 2024-25 PG information booklet.

evidence.claimText: Sri Ramachandra Hospital is a tertiary care and referral centre inside the campus with, on average, 5,000 out-patients a day; the Department of Environmental Health Engineering has been a WHO Collaborating Centre for Research and Training in Occupational Health since 2007 and started the MPH with the University of California, Berkeley; the placement cell reports nearly 700 offers through 230 campus processes with packages from Rs 2.2 lakh to Rs 72 lakh a year.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Student Manual 2026-27, pp. 43-44, 60
evidence.internalNotes: Out-patient figure from the 2024-25 PG information booklet (https://media.sriramachandra.edu/ms/storage/2024/05/pg-info-booklet-2024-1.pdf); placement figures are SRIHER-reported, not independently audited.

evidence.claimText: Hostel fees for AY 2026-27 for international students: A/C single with common bath USD 1,700 a year and USD 750 caution deposit; A/C twin sharing USD 900 and USD 375; non-A/C single USD 900 and USD 375; non-A/C twin sharing USD 450 and USD 300; payable at admission and annually thereafter, subject to availability.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), p. 20
evidence.internalNotes: Identical table in the PG 2026-27 prospectus p. 21. CCTV, biometric entry and 9 p.m. gate closure from the Student Manual 2026-27 section 9.

evidence.claimText: Canteen and mess facilities are in the hostel complexes; students pay the mess directly before hostel admission; dining only in the mess with no room service; night cafeterias in the hostels 9 p.m. to 1 a.m.; carbonated beverages and junk food banned on premises per a Department of Higher Education (MHRD) directive.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Student Manual 2026-27, sections 7.1.8 and 9.16

evidence.claimText: Foreign students must hold health insurance, charged at USD 50 a year; the on-campus hospital provides a 24x 7 emergency service with ambulance and treatment at concessional charges; SRIHER applies the UGC, MCI, DCI and AICTE anti-ragging regulations and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Ragging Act 1997 and reports NIL ragging incidents for the academic year to date.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER - Insurance / Visa for International Students; Prospectus 2026-27 FN (UG), pp. 20-21
evidence.internalNotes: Insurance charge and ragging data from https://media.sriramachandra.edu/ms/storage/2026/04/PROSPECTUS_Foreign-Nationals-Admissions-18_April_2026-compressed.pdf.

evidence.claimText: The International Relations Office handles international admissions, pre-arrival support, orientation, statutory compliance including FRRO, Bonafide Certificates and APAAR IDs for students without Aadhaar; three named student counsellors offer free confidential counselling on the 3 rd floor, IQAC wing, and every student has a faculty mentor.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Student Manual 2026-27, section 3.2; International Relation / Students page
evidence.internalNotes: IRO services also from https://sriramachandra.edu/nri-about-us/ and FN UG prospectus p. 23.

evidence.claimText: The Form II (formerly Form S) and Form III (formerly Form C) registrations of foreign nationals and their campus residence are filed with the FRRO by the university within 24 hours of admission; students with a student visa of more than 180 days register with the FRRO within 14 days of arrival; UG classes commence around the second week of July 2026 and PG classes around the third week of July 2026.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER Prospectus 2026-27 Foreign Nationals Admissions (UG), pp. 20-21; PG prospectus p. 22

evidence.claimText: The 2026-27 Foreign National and NRI undergraduate application forms are titled 'Undergraduate Admissions 2026-27... (Excluding Medical & Dental)', and the FN UG prospectus programme list does not include MBBS, BDS or B.Pharm; all fees once paid are not refunded, and students discontinuing after the cut-off date must remit fees for the entire remaining programme period.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER FN UG 2026-27 application; Prospectus 2026-27 FN (UG), pp. 1, 7, 22-23
evidence.internalNotes: MBBS omitted from the bundle for this reason: no published foreign-national route, quota or counselling authority for 2026-27. NMC facts were therefore not researched for publication.

evidence.claimText: Sri Ramachandra Faculty of Management Sciences partners with Bentley University (USA), ACCA-UK, ICMAI, XLRI, ZOHO and others, and holds NBA, ACCA-UK and ICMAI accreditations.

evidence.claimText: The NAAC valid-accreditation workbook (as on 14-08-2025, Universities sheet) records Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research, Porur, Chennai (AISHE U-0478, Track TNUNGN 10143) at Cycle 3, CGPA 3.53, Grade A++, declared 25-01-2021.
evidence.sourceLabel: NAAC - Accreditation Status register, institutions with valid accreditation
evidence.internalNotes: Supervisor regulator verification 2026-09-21 (regulator-findings-india-batch-2.md). VALIDITY CAVEAT: the standard five-year point from the January 2021 declaration fell in January 2026 and no renewal appears in any published NAAC Standing Committee result through the 265th SC of 12 Dec 2025 (no later SC results published as of 2026-09-21). Badge therefore states the declaration year only, with no currency claim; never write 'currently A++' or any valid-until date. Re-check NAAC SC results at next review.

evidence.claimText: NIRF India Rankings 2025 (Ministry of Education) place SRIHER (IR-*-I-1486) 60 th in the University category, 21 st in the Medical category, 13 th in the Dental category and 36 th in the Pharmacy category; SRIHER is not in the 2025 Overall list.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals need an Indian student visa rather than a tourist visa, postgraduate foreign-national applicants register on the Study in India portal, the university files the FRRO registrations within 24 hours of admission and students on visas longer than 180 days register with the Chennai FRRO within 14 days.
evidence.sourceLabel: SRIHER insurance and visa guidance for international students
